edo_domains: Tsu Domain (Tōdō clan, also ruling Iga)

meiji_transition.summary: In 1871 Anotsu Prefecture (north) and Watarai Prefecture (south) were set up; Anotsu was renamed Mie in 1872 and Watarai joined in 1876.
meiji_transition.boundary_note: Mie spans four provinces — Ise, Iga, Shima and eastern Kii; the Kumano area belonged to Kii and shares roots with Wakayama, so the Kumano Kodō crosses both prefectures.

history_timeline.title: The Grand Shrine and the Saikū
history_timeline.summary: Ise Grand Shrine enshrines Amaterasu, the imperial ancestor, and the court sent an imperial princess to live at the Saikū as high priestess; Shima was a 'miketsukuni'.

history_timeline.title: Ise Shintō
history_timeline.summary: After the Genpei War Ise, old Taira country, came under the shogunate; the Watarai family of the Outer Shrine developed 'Ise Shintō'.

history_timeline.title: The Kitabatake governors
history_timeline.summary: The Kitabatake, key Southern Court vassals, ruled southern Ise as provincial governors from Taki, lasting into the Sengoku period.

history_timeline.title: Ninja of Iga
history_timeline.summary: The samurai of Iga governed themselves as the 'Sōkoku Ikki' until crushed by the Oda in the 1581 Tenshō Iga War; Kuki Yoshitaka's iron-clad ships defeated the Mōri navy.

history_timeline.title: The Ise pilgrimage
history_timeline.summary: 'Once in a lifetime to Ise' became a common dream, with millions flocking there in 'okage-mairi' waves; Matsusaka merchants (the Mitsui) rose to prominence.

history_timeline.title: Pearls and industry
history_timeline.summary: Mikimoto Kōkichi succeeded in culturing pearls at Toba; the Yokkaichi petrochemical complex also caused 'Yokkaichi asthma' pollution.

landmarks.name: Meoto Iwa
landmarks.note: Wedded rocks joined by a sacred rope at Futami

specialties.name: Matsusaka beef
specialties.note: One of Japan's three great wagyu

specialties.name: Ise lobster
specialties.note: Specialty of the Shima coast and Mie’s prefectural fish

specialties.name: Akafuku mochi
specialties.note: Red-bean mochi of the Ise pilgrimage

dialect.name: Ise dialect
dialect.features: Mostly Kansai-style, ending in '-yanka' or '-damonde'; Iga speech is closer to Kyoto's.

guide.opening: I once traveled to Ise at the High Priestess's command… a thousand years ago now. The pilgrims still crowd to Ise today — shall I tell you of the Saikū, or of the Iga ninja?

regional_meme.title: Kansai or Tōkai?
regional_meme.text: Is Mie part of Kansai or Tōkai? Weather, high-school baseball and TV stations all disagree, and Mie itself is split into two camps.

regional_meme.title: Ise-pilgrimage nonchalance
regional_meme.text: 'Ise Grand Shrine is our local shrine' — Mie people watch the flood of pilgrims with a shrug.

hero_persona.name: Matsuo Bashō
hero_persona.title: Saint of haiku · born in Iga
hero_persona.opening_line: I am Matsuo Bashō, born in Iga-Ueno. Some say I must have been a ninja — how else could I walk so far in a day? Heh — shall I share a haiku?
hero_persona.tone_prompt: relaxed and wry, poetic, occasionally reciting a haiku; the 'Bashō was a ninja' theory is folklore and should be noted as such

ramen.highlight: Mie's noodle star is Ise udon; ramen here is mostly clear-broth chūka soba

sake.taste_profile: Rich & sweet: lively fruit and balanced sweet-tartness — very hard to find
